A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same low-rank Bayesian neural-network study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–I are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v2 reports original MIMIC-III, Beijing forecasting, and SST-2 experiments, plus MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and toy-regression results in Appendix I.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds SWAG evaluations, controlled computational profiling, and a low-rank ensemble study.

M1.justification: The factorized posterior, ELBO, optimization, and architecture-specific implementations in Section 2 are unchanged. Appendix H.5 adds an implemented five-member low-rank Bayesian ensemble that aggregates 20 posterior draws per member; v2 discussed low-rank ensembles only as potential future work.

E1.justification: Dataset and task coverage is retained: MIMIC-III with newborn OOD, Beijing forecasting with Guangzhou OOD, SST-2 with AG News OOD, MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and toy-regression extrapolation. The added comparisons and profiling use existing coverage.

E2.justification: SWAG changes from an acknowledged missing comparison in v2 to an evaluated posterior baseline across all three main benchmarks in Section 4.5 and Appendix H.6. This substantially extends the comparison to another scalable posterior approach. The original six-method benchmark comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v3 introduces controlled profiling with 10 warmup and 50 measured steps, a seven-configuration rank sweep, ensemble prediction aggregation, and dataset-specific SWAG training protocols. Existing reported settings also change: Beijing validation/test sizes become 6,260 rather than 7,553, and the toy uncertainty analysis changes its stated percentile range and in-domain window. These corrections do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices H.4.1–H.4.2 add controlled efficiency analysis and rank sensitivity of memory, training, and inference costs. Appendix H.5 tests whether low-rank ensembling mitigates calibration deficiencies, previously only hypothesized. Existing predictive rank ablations, initialization comparisons, calibration-bin checks, and OOD analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 2 first displays standard deviations for the existing four-run Beijing results, previously shown as means alone. Figure 6 changes its seed count from five to four, and Appendix G.1 narrows the general repeated-run statement to main-text experiments. New profiling and ensemble studies explicitly disclose single-run limitations; no increase in runs for retained results is established.

E6.justification: New results include controlled profiling and rank-sweep measurements, the ensemble's 0.731 OOD AUROC and 0.415 NLL in Table 17, and SWAG outcomes in Tables 18–20. Existing values also change: low-rank Beijing MAE at 100% retention changes from 10.55 to 10.63 between v2 Table 11 and v3 Table 12, while Table 3 changes Rank-1 AUPR-In from 0.272 to 0.271. Most original benchmark scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.4 receives a direct null-support proof of singularity. Theorem 3.7 corrects its tail-error term from the sum of squared singular values to its square root, matching the retained appendix proof. Appendix C.5 restricts the 1-Lipschitz MAE statement to scalar outputs and corrects MSE smoothness from two to one. The broader theoretical framework and generalization proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract changes the maximum parameter-saving claim from 15-fold to 33-fold, already reported for SST-2 in v2's body, and explicitly acknowledges Deep Ensembles' likelihood advantages. The conclusion replaces a consistent calibration–OOD tradeoff with a task-dependent claim. The central low-rank variational and theoretical contributions remain.

C2.justification: Sections 4.6 and H.1 replace a uniform OOD-superiority interpretation with task-specific tradeoffs. v3 withdraws the description of 0.790 coverage as near 95%, distinguishes interval-calibration AUC from ECE and point accuracy from calibration, and corrects MNIST/Fashion-MNIST ranking interpretations. It also explains moderate runtime scaling and explicitly qualifies the supplementary ensemble and recovered rank-sweep evidence.

D1.justification: Appendices G.5.4 and H.5–H.6 add substantial reproducibility information: profiling hardware and memory-measurement API, warmup and measurement budgets, optimizer distinctions, ensemble sampling, and SWAG training phases, ranks, seeds, and posterior-sample counts. Existing documentation clarifies parameter accounting and experiment-specific Monte Carlo counts. MNIST's stated scaling range is corrected while retaining division by 126, rather than documenting a new preprocessing operation.

R1.justification: The introduction and new Appendix A.6 substantially broaden positioning against reduced-rank regression, probabilistic/Bayesian matrix factorization, deterministic compression, and function-space or post-training uncertainty methods. New Watanabe references distinguish measure-theoretic singularity from singular learning theory. SWAG also receives a citation and substantive empirical positioning.

P1.justification: v3 makes focused rewrites in the abstract, results discussion, conclusion, and appendix interpretations, expands the running title, and introduces subsections for the added material. The overall narrative sequence, methods organization, and Appendix A–I structure remain intact.

P2.justification: The tabular presentation expands substantially with profiling, rank-sweep, ensemble, and SWAG tables. Main-text Table 4 redisplays a subset of Appendix Table 13. Table 2 gains standard-deviation formatting, and several captions and placements change. Figures 1–20 retain their underlying plots; their relocation is not new experimental evidence.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the central efficiency and uncertainty arguments. SWAG evaluations address an explicitly acknowledged comparison gap, while matched profiling separates modest epoch-time gains from larger parameter and memory savings. Mathematical corrections and task-specific interpretations repair misleading statements in v2. The additions remain limited by single-run profiling and ensemble evidence, differing SST-2 reference values, and unchanged percentage improvements accompanying corrected MAEs in Table 12. These issues constrain confidence but do not outweigh the substantial gains in supporting evidence and accuracy of interpretation.
